TheOneConvert: Turn Any Public Article URL into Markdown / PDF / EPUB - with One Clean TypeScript UI
To simplify complications is the first essential of success. — George E. E. H. Moore
I started with one very practical pain: Medium exports everything, but I often only need one article - cleanly - so I can store it in GitHub, ship it as a PDF, or bundle it into an EPUB. That small “one-article export” itch turned into a bigger idea: paste any public article URL, extract the readable content, and export it to the formats I actually use - Markdown, HTML, PDF, EPUB, TXT - with no tracking, and the whole thing open-sourced.
That’s what TheOneConvert is: one input box, one click, one output.
Source: https://github.com/dorangao/theoneconvert No tracking. No URL logs. No analytics. Just convert.
What It Does
Paste any public article URL (Medium friend links included). The app:
•
Fetches the HTML
•
Extracts the “readable article” (removes nav, ads, unrelated layout)
•
Normalizes the content into a single canonical form
•
Exports to:
•
Markdown (.md)
•
HTML (.html)
•
PDF (.pdf)
•
EPUB (.epub)
•
TXT (.txt)
The UI stays intentionally minimal: one URL input, format picker, and a download button.
The Architecture
The core philosophy: server does the heavy lifting, client stays dumb/simple.
Key Design Choices (The “Why”)
1) Canonical HTML first
Everything becomes “clean article HTML” first. From there:
•
Markdown is deterministic
•
TXT is derived from Markdown
•
PDF/EPUB rendering is consistent
2) Readability extraction
Most webpages are hostile to conversion (ads, sidebars, infinite scroll). The converter extracts only what a human would call “the article”.
3) No tracking, no URL logs
You don’t want your “reading list” or internal links stored anywhere. This project doesn’t need that data to work - so it never collects it.
Implementation Overview (TypeScript + Next.js)
This is a simple Next.js app:
•
app/page.tsx → minimalist UI
•
app/api/convert/route.ts → conversion pipeline (server)
•
lib/convert/* → format-specific exporters
Dependencies (typical picks)
•
jsdom + @mozilla/readability for article extraction
•
turndown for HTML → Markdown
•
playwright for HTML → PDF
•
epub-gen (or similar) for EPUB packaging
The Minimal UI (One URL, One Button)
app/page.tsx (core idea, simplified)
"use client"; import { useState } from "react"; type Format = "md" | "html" | "pdf" | "epub" | "txt"; export default function Home() { const [url, setUrl] = useState(""); const [format, setFormat] = useState("md"); const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false); const [error, setError] = useState(null); async function convert() { setLoading(true); setError(null); try { const res = await fetch("/api/convert", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ url, format }), }); if (!res.ok) { const msg = await res.text(); throw new Error(msg || "Conversion failed"); } const blob = await res.blob(); const filename = res.headers.get("X-Filename") ?? `theoneconvert.${format}`; const a = document.createElement("a"); a.href = URL.createObjectURL(blob); a.download = filename; a.click(); URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href); } catch (e: any) { setError(e.message ?? "Unknown error"); } finally { setLoading(false); } } return ( TheOneConvert Paste any public article URL → export Markdown, HTML, PDF, EPUB, or TXT. No tracking. setUrl(e.target.value)} placeholder="Paste article URL..." style={{ flex: 1, padding: 10, borderRadius: 10, border: "1px solid #ddd" }} /> setFormat(e.target.value as Format)} style={{ padding: 10, borderRadius: 10, border: "1px solid #ddd" }} > {loading ? "Converting..." : "Convert"} {error &amp;&amp; ( {error} )} ); }
That’s the whole UI: one job, one flow.
The Server API Route (The Pipeline)
app/api/convert/route.ts (core logic, simplified but real)
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server"; import { JSDOM } from "jsdom"; import { Readability } from "@mozilla/readability"; import TurndownService from "turndown"; import { renderPdfFromHtml } from "@/lib/convert/pdf"; import { renderEpubFromHtml } from "@/lib/convert/epub"; export const runtime = "nodejs"; // needed for jsdom/playwright/epub-gen type Format = "md" | "html" | "pdf" | "epub" | "txt"; function normalizeFilename(title: string, ext: string) { const safe = title .toLowerCase() .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-") .replace(/^-|-$/g, "") .slice(0, 80); return `${safe || "theoneconvert"}.${ext}`; } async function fetchHtml(url: string) { const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { // many sites return better HTML with a browser UA "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome Safari", Accept: "text/html,*/*", }, redirect: "follow", }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Fetch failed (${res.status})`); return await res.text(); } function extractArticle(html: string, url: string) { const dom = new JSDOM(html, { url }); const reader = new Readability(dom.window.document); const article = reader.parse(); if (!article?.content) { throw new Error("Could not extract readable article content."); } const title = article.title || "theoneconvert"; const contentHtml = article.content; // main article HTML return { title, contentHtml }; } function htmlToMarkdown(contentHtml: string) { const turndown = new TurndownService({ codeBlockStyle: "fenced", headingStyle: "atx", }); // Keep blocks clean turndown.addRule("fencedCodeBlock", { filter: (node) => node.nodeName === "PRE" &amp;&amp; node.firstChild &amp;&amp; (node.firstChild as any).nodeName === "CODE", replacement: (content, node) => { const code = (node.textContent || "").replace(/ $/, ""); return ` \`\`\` ${code} \`\`\` `; }, }); return turndown.turndown(contentHtml); } export async function POST(req: NextRequest) { const { url, format } = (await req.json()) as { url: string; format: Format }; if (!url || !/^https?:\/\//.test(url)) { return new NextResponse("Invalid URL", { status: 400 }); } const html = await fetchHtml(url); const { title, contentHtml } = extractArticle(html, url); // canonical standalone HTML const standaloneHtml = ` ${title} ${contentHtml}`; let body: Buffer; let ext: string; let contentType: string; switch (format) { case "html": body = Buffer.from(standaloneHtml, "utf-8"); ext = "html"; contentType = "text/html; charset=utf-8"; break; case "md": { const md = htmlToMarkdown(contentHtml); body = Buffer.from(md, "utf-8"); ext = "md"; contentType = "text/markdown; charset=utf-8"; break; } case "txt": { const md = htmlToMarkdown(contentHtml); // simple txt: strip markdown formatting lightly (keep readable) const txt = md .replace(/```[\s\S]*?```/g, (m) => m.replace(/```/g, "")) // keep code text .replace(/[#>*_`]/g, "") .trim(); body = Buffer.from(txt, "utf-8"); ext = "txt"; contentType = "text/plain; charset=utf-8"; break; } case "pdf": { const pdf = await renderPdfFromHtml(standaloneHtml); body = pdf; ext = "pdf"; contentType = "application/pdf"; break; } case "epub": { const epub = await renderEpubFromHtml({ title, html: contentHtml, sourceUrl: url }); body = epub; ext = "epub"; contentType = "application/epub+zip"; break; } default: return new NextResponse("Unsupported format", { status: 400 }); } const filename = normalizeFilename(title, ext); return new NextResponse(body, { status: 200, headers: { "Content-Type": contentType, "Content-Disposition": `attachment; filename="${filename}"`, "X-Filename": filename, // no tracking headers, no logs - keep it simple }, }); }
That’s the whole concept: fetch → extract → canonical HTML → export.
PDF Export (Playwright)
lib/convert/pdf.ts (the critical part)
import { chromium } from "playwright"; export async function renderPdfFromHtml(html: string): Promise { const browser = await chromium.launch(); const page = await browser.newPage(); // Load HTML directly (no external navigation needed) await page.setContent(html, { waitUntil: "domcontentloaded" }); const pdf = await page.pdf({ format: "A4", printBackground: true, margin: { top: "18mm", bottom: "18mm", left: "14mm", right: "14mm" }, }); await browser.close(); return Buffer.from(pdf); }
If your article has heavy code blocks, this PDF output tends to be much cleaner than “browser print”.
EPUB Export (Readable on Kindle / Books)
lib/convert/epub.ts (simple packaging)
import Epub from "epub-gen"; export async function renderEpubFromHtml(args: { title: string; html: string; sourceUrl: string; }): Promise { const options = { title: args.title, author: "TheOneConvert", content: [ { title: args.title, data: `${args.html}Source: ${args.sourceUrl}`, }, ], }; // epub-gen writes to file by default, so we use a temp file then read back const tmp = `/tmp/theoneconvert-${Date.now()}.epub`; await new Epub(options, tmp).promise; const fs = await import("node:fs/promises"); return await fs.readFile(tmp); }
Practical Notes (So It Doesn’t Break in the Real World)
•
Some sites block server fetches. If that happens, add:
•
a simple “fetch proxy” with better headers
•
optional user-provided cookies (advanced)
•
Images: you can keep images as remote URLs (simplest) or download and embed for EPUB (more work)
•
Tables: Markdown tables sometimes degrade; canonical HTML stays best
Why This Matters (For Builders)
I keep coming back to the same pattern: the internet is full of knowledge, but it’s locked in formats that are inconvenient for building.
Markdown is the developer’s storage format. PDF is the universal sharing format. EPUB is the portable reading format.
When conversion becomes one clean UI action, you stop “saving links” and start building your own library.
